tr.td: Establishing primary care for Parkinson's disease: motor, non-motor, fall-risk, and orthostatic assessment
Four-week follow-up with movement disorders neurology consultation for levodopa adjustment and rehabilitation
Three-month Parkinson's disease review after the levodopa increase and speech therapy

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Review the levodopa dose and timing at every visit for slowness, wearing-off, and dyskinesia; take doses 30 minutes before meals; check supine and three-minute standing blood pressure after any change; avoid dopamine-blocking drugs such as metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, and most antipsychotics
Movement disorders neurology consultation to confirm the diagnosis against the MDS criteria, adjust levodopa, plan rehabilitation, and advise on genetic testing
Four-week intensive speech therapy (LSVT LOUD) for soft speech, and physical therapy for gait, balance, and a home exercise program of at least 150 minutes a week

Monitor on the CMID schedule: motor examination, Hoehn and Yahr stage, fall check, psychosis and impulse-control questions, and medication review every visit; cognition, mood, sleep, autonomic symptoms, swallowing, speech, and driving yearly; dental examination every six months
Advance care planning: name a health care agent and record goals of care, and revisit with any change in stage
Less slowness of movement after a levodopa adjustment, without dyskinesia or orthostatic hypotension, by the three-month review
MDS-UPDRS Part III fell from 30 to 24; no dyskinesia; no orthostatic hypotension
Complete a four-week intensive speech therapy course and keep up daily voice practice
LSVT LOUD course completed; easier to hear in conversation; daily home practice continues
No falls through the six-month review, with at least 150 minutes a week of exercise including balance work
No falls; Timed Up and Go improved from 13 to 11 seconds; exercising about 180 minutes a week

Falls: none in the past year and no near falls; Timed Up and Go 13 seconds without an aid [S]
Orthostatic check at the first visit: 130/80 mmHg, pulse 70, after 5 minutes supine; 122/78 mmHg, pulse 76, after 3 minutes standing, without symptoms; no orthostatic hypotension [S]

Non-motor screens at the first visit: EAT-10 swallowing screen 2 (below the threshold of 3), no choking or coughing with meals; no dream enactment on the RBD screening questionnaire; Epworth Sleepiness Scale 6; no constipation, urinary urgency, or lightheadedness; no hallucinations; impulse-control screen (QUIP-RS) negative [S]
Independent in all activities of daily living; buttoning and handwriting are slow; drives only short local trips in daylight [S]
